page: The Microsoft Azure E96ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading running at frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. The compute architecture features an x86_64 instruction set with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA_NI. The instance is allocated 672 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Integrated directly into the host hardware, the E96ads_v6 includes 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, bypassing network-attached storage latency for high-speed scratch space and temporary file operations. The virtual machine runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent external disk arrays. No hardware GPUs are provisioned on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier compute and memory access capability. Multi-core execution via stress-ng achieved a score of 147,511.51, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems, while single-core performance registered at 3,077.18 in the top 25%. In memory-centric key-value testing, the instance delivered 112.8 million Redis SET operations per second, reflecting high sustained data ingestion capabilities.

By delivering massive memory alongside 5.67 TB of fast local NVMe capacity, the E96ads_v6 achieves strong resource density and operational efficiency for scaled data tiers. The omission of dedicated GPUs directs all compute resources strictly toward CPU-bound and memory-bound tasks. This virtual machine is engineered for large-scale relational and in-memory databases, real-time analytical processing, Redis caching deployments, and intensive ETL pipelines.

Storage architecture features a bundled 5670 GB local NVMe SSD array alongside Premium Storage support, while GPU hardware is omitted. The instance delivers high resource density for memory-heavy computing without external storage latency penalties. It is suitable for hosting large in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput data transformation pipelines.
